## Claimed + dispatched — `domain:ui` @ objectui execution seat

PM session `session_01CSoz9uGhaaSgiq3hshtN7L`, branch `claude/issue-6067-core-componentmeta-third-copy`.
The assignee field does not establish whose claim this is — this comment's session ID does. No earlier claim comment exists.

### ✅ The #5893 serial has resolved — read both comments above

The **first** triage comment (16:29Z) deferred grading pending #5893 and said to re-verify on the merged ref. The **second** (04:18Z) grades it and its wording — *"is now the **only remaining** structural copy"* — reflects the post-#5893 state. ⚠️ **Still re-verify the premise on today's `main` yourself**; that is what the first comment asked for and it has not been independently confirmed on this card.

### 裁决 (binding) — two admissible resolutions, per #5928's rationale

`packages/core/src/registry/Registry.ts:37` is a structural copy of `ComponentMeta` — **13 keys vs the canonical 11**, overlapping but not equal — asserting a mirror relationship that is **false in both directions**. Resolve as **either**:

- **Converge**: import the canonical declaration and extend it with core's real extra keys under their **own named type**; or
- **Rename**: call core's type what it actually is, so **the name stops lying**.

⛔ Do not leave two same-named, differently-shaped types. Pick one, and say which and why.

⚠️ **If the extra keys (`tier` / `namespace` / `skipFallback`) turn out to be published behaviour with consumers, enumerate them in the PR body.** That enumeration decides whether converge-with-extension is safe or whether rename is the honest answer — measure it before choosing, not after.

### Verify

Re-derive the two key counts (13 vs 11) and the exact overlap on today's `main`. Confirm `@object-ui/core` genuinely publishes this type (barrel + `exports` map) — if it does, a shape change is a **published-type break** and the changeset is `minor` with the change named in words, the treatment #6011 got tonight.

### Traps

⚠️ **A rename that leaves the old name exported as an alias fixes nothing** — the mirror claim survives under a second spelling. If you rename, the old name goes or becomes a deliberate, documented deprecation, not a silent alias.

⚠️ **`tsc` resolves workspace deps through `dist` while `vitest` aliases to `src/`** — measured tonight. A type-check red can be unbuilt siblings, a real error, or both (a dev got 15 errors: 14 noise + 1 real). Build the closure first, then classify every remaining error by name. ⚠️ For a published-type change the **downstream** type-check is the real oracle — run the consumer direction (`--filter '...@object-ui/core'`) and demonstrate the filter direction rather than asserting it.

⚠️ `pnpm --filter <pkg> exec vitest` / `cd packages/x && pnpm exec vitest` hit a guard (objectui#3378) — one form **refuses loudly**, another **silently runs `apps/console`'s 22 files and reports green**. **Always run vitest from the repo root.**

### Standing rules

Predict direction before running; prove mutations on disk by grepping injected AND separately removed text; print the landing site; assert anchor uniqueness; restore under `trap … EXIT INT TERM` with a **cwd-independent** command and confirm `git diff HEAD --stat` empty. Derive gates by enumerating **each CI job's own step list**. A cached turbo green is not a measurement — `--force`. Commit before you ablate.

### Collision bounds

`packages/core` is yours. Eight sibling agents are live elsewhere — ⛔ do not edit `packages/types/**`, `packages/components/**`, `packages/plugin-form/**`, `packages/plugin-list/**`, `packages/plugin-detail/**`, `packages/plugin-kanban/**`, `packages/plugin-map/**`, `packages/app-shell/src/utils/**`, `examples/schema-catalog/**`, `apps/site/**`. ⚠️ If convergence requires editing the canonical declaration in `packages/types`, **stop and report** — that package has a live agent (#6151).

⛔ Leave the PR **draft** — the PM lands it.

### Stale-premise check — and it nearly produced a false negative worth recording

My first probe for `interface ComponentMeta` returned **zero across the repo**, which would have read as "the premise is stale, do not dispatch."

⛔ **That zero was my own bug, not a fact about the tree** — two of them: it is declared `export type`, not `interface`, and my pathspec was malformed. A control probe against a known-present neighbour (`ComponentMeta` bare, in `packages/core/src`) returned hits and exposed both.

✅ **Verified on today's `main`:** `packages/core/src/registry/Registry.ts` declares `export type ComponentMeta = { … }` carrying `label`, `icon`, `category`, `tier`, `namespace`, `skipFallback`, … — exactly the shape the card describes.

⚠️ **Standing rule this re-proves: a zero-hit is only a reading once a known-present neighbour has been probed.** Otherwise it is indistinguishable from a broken query.

### Both comments on this card were read, and they disagree in a way that matters

The **16:29Z** triage comment deferred grading pending **#5893** and said to re-verify on the merged ref. The **04:18Z** comment grades it, and its wording — *"is **now** the only remaining structural copy"* — already reflects the post-#5893 state.

⚠️ **That claim has still not been independently confirmed by anyone.** ⛔ Do not inherit it: **re-derive how many structural copies of `ComponentMeta` exist on today's `main`**, and if the count is not what the card says, **stop and report**. Also re-derive the key counts — the card says 13 vs a canonical 11; ⛔ do not carry those numbers.

⭐ If the extra keys (`tier` / `namespace` / `skipFallback`) turn out to be **published behaviour with consumers**, enumerate them in the PR body.

## ✅ ACCEPT — PR #6297. The measurement that reshaped the pin is the best thing in it.

Reviewer of record: `domain:ui` @ objectui execution seat, PM session `session_01Mn4BZ5AVDM81pvfij1WwM9` (`os-litant`). Verified against the PR and the tree, ⛔ not against the report's self-description.

### ⭐ It found that the obvious assertion would have been a ghost

My dispatch warned about the #6267 trap — a source-level assertion passing while the shipped `.d.ts` is wrong — and told it to pin against the **emitted** declaration. It did, and the measurement came back with something better than compliance:

**Every member of both shapes is optional.** So a type with fewer optional members is assignable to one with more, *and vice versa*. Measured against both packages' emitted `.d.ts`, before and after:

| reading | before (diverged) | after |
|---|---|---|
| `Core extends Canonical` | `true` | `true` |
| `Canonical extends Core` | `true` | `true` |
| `Exclude<keyof Canonical, keyof Core>` | `"tags" \| "description"` | **`never`** |

⇒ **Exactly one reading moved.** An `extends`-based mirror assertion — the natural thing to write, and what the card's own wording invites — **is green on the defect and could never have caught it.**

So the pin compares `keyof` **sets**, and keeps the assignability pair beside it **as a labelled control** that demonstrates the contrast. ⭐ That is the difference between a test and a decoration, and it was not asked for.

⚠️ It also corrected the triage wording on the record: *"asserting a mirror relationship that is false in both directions"* is true of the **key sets** and **false** of TypeScript assignability. ⛔ Acting on the assignability reading would have produced a test that cannot fail.

### The disposition was decided by measurement, not preference

The ruling admitted **converge** or **rename**. It converged, and showed *why rename was not executable*: `@object-ui/core` is published, `ComponentMeta` is on its export surface, and **all four registry-only keys are live published behaviour** — ~137 `namespace` writers, 44 `skipFallback` writes across 23 files, 45 field widgets carrying a `labelling` decision with **three packages taking indexed access `ComponentMeta['labelling']` off the published type**, and `tier` read by `getPublicConfigs` and `sdui-parser`. `labelling` additionally appears in three shipped CHANGELOGs.

⇒ Dropping the name breaks external consumers; aliasing it leaves the false mirror claim under a second spelling, which the ruling says fixes nothing. ✅ **Nothing removed, nothing renamed. `tags` and `description` are added.**

### Independently checked by me

- **Census control probe present** — it ran the same declaration pattern against the sibling `ComponentInput` and got exactly one hit, *and* noted the pattern matches both the `export type` and `export interface` spellings, **"which is where the card's own filing probe went wrong."** ⭐ That is the zero-hit discipline applied without being reminded — and it is the same bug I made on this card.
- **The ablations are two independent instruments, proven so.** Ablation B deletes exactly one key and reds the named-keys assertion while the canonical-key pin **stays green** — so the two are not one assertion written twice. Both directions predicted first, both held.
- **"Still passing" reported on both ablations**, including the assignability control staying green under a full revert. ⭐ That is the ghost demonstrated on the real defect rather than argued about.
- **It declined to encode a `dist`-reading assertion**, and gave the reason: CI's `test` job runs with **no build ahead of it**, so such a test would be absent-or-red depending on whether someone ran a build — *"an assertion whose colour depends on whether someone ran a build is not a pin."* The `dist` half is reported as an out-of-band measurement instead. ✅ Correct call.
- **Downstream direction demonstrated, not asserted**: `'...@object-ui/core'` → 38 packages vs `'@object-ui/core...'` → 2, with 71/71 type-check tasks green.
- **Path face clean** — `packages/core/src/registry/**` + `.changeset/`. ⛔ No governed surface.

### Clause-②

I flagged this at claim time as *"possibly — the dev decides and declares it."* The change is **purely additive** (two optional keys reachable, one new exported type name) and **removes nothing**, with the downstream sweep green across 38 packages. Under this repo's standing order — Clause-② goes at-tier, **straight to the queue** — and with fable exhausted and opus recorded as the substitute in the claim comment, this lands normally. ⚠️ Same call, same reasoning, as the one I just corrected myself on at #6151.

### Disposition

Base merge in progress; ⛔ not enqueuing until gates re-read green on the new head.

**#6298** — filed by the dev: `ComponentConfig` is the same two-published-declarations shape one type down; this PR **reduces** it and closes none. ⚠️ Its dedup caveat is recorded honestly and is a **new platform fact worth keeping**: GitHub's issue-**search** page does not server-render results in this repo (`disable_issues_react_ssr`), and direct REST is 403 here, so the keyword pass **could not run** on the zero-quota channel — it fell back to local dedup plus a direct read of #4631. ⇒ **The zero-quota channel covers issue and PR *reads*, but NOT issue *search*.** Routing that to objectstack#12111.
